You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

Workspace: JacobianChallenge
Project: Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
Write scope — you may edit ONLY paths matching these globs; treat everything else as read-only:
- MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/**
- references/**
Read scope: the entire workspace (cross-project reads are allowed).
Log/artifact directory: .archon-horizon/runs/0020/sessions/0014-horizon-T15

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, hold a 1-to-1 correspondence with the Lean, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

- **Critical path** (in order): (1) ~~real relative Pic presheaf~~ DONE session 0015 (`PicSharp.relPresheaf` in `RelPicFunctor.lean`, `H_T`-coset carrier, axiom-clean); (2) étale sheafification target — Mathlib v4.31 has NO étale Grothendieck topology on schemes; either parametrize or use Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5: for C/k with a **k-rational section**, `Pic^♯(T) → Pic^♯_ét(T)` is already bijective, so representability can be stated against `relPresheaf` directly under a section hypothesis; (3) rewire FGA `picSharp` := (sheafified) relative functor — universe bump `Type u → Type (u+1)` in `HasPicSharp`/`HasPicScheme` is viable (`Functor.RepresentableBy` is universe-polymorphic; `Equiv` is cross-universe); (4) `Pic(C_ε) ≅ H¹(C_ε, O^×)` cocycle classification + truncated exponential split sequence `0 → O_C → O^×_{C_ε} → O^×_C → 1` for the kernel = `H¹(C,O_C)` computation (Kleiman Thm 5.11) — none of this exists yet, largest remaining block.
- **TRAP**: wiring `picSharp := PicSharp.presheaf` (the absolute functor, iso-class carrier) would make `PicSharpRepresentable`'s sorry a mathematically FALSE statement (absolute `Pic(C×T)` is not representable — it differs from `Hom(T, Pic)` by `Pic(T)`). - Proof-pattern notes: the `Quotient.lift`/`Quotient.sound` + iso-chain style (pullbackCongr/pullbackId/pullbackComp `.app`, D4′ `pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial`, `pullback_pullback_eq`) compiled essentially first-try — no v4.31 transparency walls in this corner. `pullback.lift_fst/snd` are NOT simp (only `@[reassoc]`); pass them + their `_assoc` forms to `simp` explicitly after `pullback.hom_ext`.

For a genus-$\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/étale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now — record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.

**Caveat 2 — `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free ℤ/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, étale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.
- **`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.

39	## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (route (b))
40	
41	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
42	Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
43	schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
44	`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
45	for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps
46	
47	```
48	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
49	```
50	
51	are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
52	(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
53	itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
54	— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is NOT
55	representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
56	the representability sorry `instHasPicScheme` below is **conditional on
57	`[HasRationalPoint C]`**: an unconditional instance would assert a false
58	statement. (Run-0008 memory `I-0061`: the same trap ruled out wiring
59	`picSharp` to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.)

331	/-! ### The substantive Abel map (run-0011 closure)
332	
333	The former `⟨sorry⟩`-backed `Nonempty (divFunctor C ⟶ picSharp C)` carrier is
334	replaced by the **explicit** natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`, and the
335	class `HasAbelMap` is repinned to **carry the map itself** (a data field
336	`abel`, no longer a bare `Prop`), so that `abelMap` acquires a genuine defining
337	property (`abelMap_app_mk` below) rather than being an opaque `Classical.choice`
338	of a `Nonempty`.
339	
340	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
341	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
342	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
343	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
344	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
345	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
346	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
347	negation on the group-valued functor.
348	
349	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
350	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
351	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
352	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
353	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
354	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
355	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
356	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
357	
358	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
359	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
360	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
361	naturality rest only on the (landed) kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
362	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
363	
364	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
365	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
366	representability (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`) is NOT claimed here. -/
367	
368	/-- Well-definedness of the ideal-class assignment `⟨F, q⟩ ↦ [ker q]` on the
369	divisor equivalence relation `DivFamily.Rel`: an equivalence `f : x.F ≅ y.F`
370	with `x.q ≫ f.hom = y.q` gives `ker x.q ≅ ker y.q` (`kernelCompMono` at the
371	iso `f.hom`), hence equal `H_T`-coset classes (`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/
372	private theorem abelKernel_welldef {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
373	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) {x y : DivFamily C.hom T.unop} (h : x.Rel y) :
374	    Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
375	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) =
376	      Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
377	        (⟨kernel y.q, y.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ : LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) := by
378	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
379	  exact Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
380	    ⟨(kernelCompMono x.q f.hom).symm ≪≫ Limits.kernelIsoOfEq hf⟩)
381	
382	/-- **Kernel commutes with base change for a divisor family** (the mathematical
383	heart of Abel-map naturality).  For a test map `g : T ⟶ T'` and a divisor family
384	`x` over `T`, the ideal of the pulled-back family is the pullback of the ideal:
385	`ker((g_C^* x).q) ≅ g_C^*(ker x.q)`.  Proof: `(pullbackAlong g.unop x).q` is
386	`triangleIso.inv ≫ g_C^*(x.q)`, so its kernel agrees with `ker(g_C^* x.q)`
387	(`kernelIsIsoComp`, precomposition by the iso `triangleIso.inv`); the
388	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
389	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
390	side hypotheses are exactly the `DivFamily` fields `epi`, quasi-coherent source,
391	`isFinitePresentation`, `flat`, `kerLocallyTrivial` over the cartesian
392	`quotBaseSquare`). -/
393	private noncomputable def abelKernelBaseChangeIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
394	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
395	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T') (x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop) :
396	    kernel ((DivFamily.pullbackAlong g.unop x).q) ≅
397	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).obj (kernel x.q) := by
398	  haveI hiso : IsIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop) x.q) :=
399	    Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseSquare C.hom g.unop) x.q x.epi
400	      (pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (pullback.fst C.hom T.unop.hom)
401	        (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf) inferInstance)
402	      x.isFinitePresentation x.flat x.kerLocallyTrivial
403	  exact kernelIsIsoComp
404	      (pullbackTriangleIso (quotBaseMap_fst C.hom g.unop)
405	        (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf)).inv
406	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop)).map x.q) ≪≫
407	    (asIso (Modules.pullbackKernelComparison (quotBaseMap C.hom g.unop) x.q)).symm

411	objects it is `⟦⟨F, q⟩⟧ ↦ ⟦ker q⟧`; naturality is the invertible
412	kernel–pullback comparison over the cartesian base-change square
413	(`abelKernelBaseChangeIso`, fed by the `DivFamily` fields).  Well-definedness on

415	noncomputable def abelKernelNatTrans {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
416	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :

9	# Genus finiteness of the curve (node `N12`, the adelic lane's consumable)
10	
11	This file is part of the **adelic Riemann–Roch lane**.  It composes the two halves
12	of the lane that are now proved:
13	
14	* the **keystone** `Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map`
15	  (`FinitenessP1.lean`, node `N11`): under the gates `HasFiniteMapToP1 C` and
16	  `P1HasLaurentChartData k`, *some* 2-affine cover `S` of `C` (the pullback of the
17	  standard ℙ¹ charts along the finite map) has finite-dimensional Čech cokernel
18	  `Ȟ¹ = S.H1Cok`, so any comparison `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₗ[k] S.H1Cok` transports the
19	  finiteness to the genus carrier;
20	* the **comparison** `AffineCoverMVSquare.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok`
21	  (`Cokernel.lean`, nodes `N5` + `N6`): for *every* 2-affine cover `S`, under the
22	  Čech-to-derived gate `HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily`,
23	  `HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1 ≃ₗ[k] S.H1Cok (toModuleKSheaf C)` — the N5 half
24	  (`cechCohomology 1 ≃ₗ H1Cok`) is unconditional, only the N6 half is gated.
25	
26	## The honest gate set
27	
28	The keystone produces an *existential* cover (`D.pullbackSquare π` for a chosen
29	finite `π` and chart data `D`), which cannot be named in a theorem signature; the
30	comparison must therefore be available for **all** 2-affine covers, i.e. the honest
31	Čech-to-derived hypothesis is the `∀`-quantified instance gate
32	`[∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily]` (a `Prop`-class
33	hypothesis with no sorried instance, in the `HasPicScheme`/`HasFiniteMapToP1`
34	gating pattern).  The full gate set of the consumable is
35	
36	* `HasFiniteMapToP1 C` — node `N9`; derived in `FiniteMapToP1.lean` from the single
37	  strictly weaker gate `ExistsNonconstantMapToP1 C` under the ambient curve
38	  hypotheses;
39	* `P1HasLaurentChartData k` — node `N11b`, the ℙ¹ chart-ring computation
40	  (`P1ChartData.lean` is building towards its instance);
41	* `HasExt.{u}`/`HasExt.{u+1}` — the ambient `Ext`-theory instances the `HModule`
42	  machinery runs on;
43	* `∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily` — the Čech-to-derived
44	  comparison (Leray/Cartan) for 2-affine covers of the curve.
45	
46	Under these, the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1` is a
47	finite-dimensional `k`-vector space, so `genus C = finrank k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is an
48	honest natural number.
49	-/

52	
53	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
56	
57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
58	
59	/-- **Genus finiteness of the curve (node `N12`, gated).**  For a curve `C` over `k`
60	with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ and the ℙ¹ chart data, and with the Čech-to-derived
61	comparison available on 2-affine covers, the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite
62	`k`-module.  Composes the `N11` keystone `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map`
63	with the `N5`+`N6` comparison `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok` of `Cokernel.lean`. -/
64	theorem module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1
65	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] [P1HasLaurentChartData k]
66	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
67	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
68	    [∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
69	      HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily] :
70	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) :=

76	
77	/-- The restriction of `T : Over S` to an open `W ⊆ T.left`, as an object of
78	`Over S`. -/
79	noncomputable def overRes {S : Scheme.{0}} (T : Over S) (W : T.left.Opens) :
80	    Over S :=
81	  Over.mk (W.ι ≫ T.hom)
82	
83	/-- The restriction morphism `T|_W ⟶ T` in `Over S`. -/
84	noncomputable def overResHom {S : Scheme.{0}} (T : Over S) (W : T.left.Opens) :
85	    overRes T W ⟶ T :=
86	  Over.homMk W.ι rfl
87	
88	/-- The inclusion `T|_{W'} ⟶ T|_W` in `Over S` attached to `W' ≤ W`. -/
89	noncomputable def overResLE {S : Scheme.{0}} (T : Over S)
90	    {W' W : T.left.Opens} (h : W' ≤ W) : overRes T W' ⟶ overRes T W :=
91	  Over.homMk (T.left.homOfLE h)
92	    ((Category.assoc _ _ _).symm.trans
93	      (congrArg (· ≫ T.hom) (T.left.homOfLE_ι h)))
94	
95	/-- **The Zariski sheaf axiom for a presheaf on `Sch/S`**: for every
96	`T : Over S` and every open cover `{W k}` of the total space `T.left`, a
97	family of sections of `F` over the restrictions `T|_{W k}` that agree on the
98	pairwise intersections glues to a unique section over `T`.  This is the sheaf
99	condition for the (big) Zariski site of `S`, stated concretely against open
100	covers of the total space; representable presheaves satisfy it, and it is the
101	hypothesis under which local representability descends
102	(`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`). -/
103	def IsZariskiSheafOver {S : Scheme.{0}} (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1) : Prop :=
104	  ∀ (T : Over S) {κ : Type} (W : κ → T.left.Opens), (⨆ k, W k = ⊤) →
105	    ∀ x : ∀ k, F.obj (Opposite.op (overRes T (W k))),
106	    (∀ k l : κ, F.map (overResLE T (inf_le_left : W k ⊓ W l ≤ W k)).op (x k)
107	      = F.map (overResLE T (inf_le_right : W k ⊓ W l ≤ W l)).op (x l)) →
108	    ∃! x₀ : F.obj (Opposite.op T), ∀ k, F.map (overResHom T (W k)).op x₀ = x k
109	
110	/-! ## §2. Generic helpers -/
111	
112	/-- A commutative square of `Type`-valued presheaves that is a pointwise
113	pullback is a pullback square (evaluation functors jointly reflect limits). -/
114	lemma isPullback_of_app {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
115	    {P X Y Z : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} {fst : P ⟶ X} {snd : P ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Z} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
116	    (h : ∀ c : Cᵒᵖ, IsPullback (fst.app c) (snd.app c) (f.app c) (g.app c)) :
117	    IsPullback fst snd f g := by
118	  have w : fst ≫ f = snd ≫ g := by
119	    apply NatTrans.ext; funext c
120	    rw [NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.comp_app]
121	    exact (h c).w
122	  exact
123	    { w := w
124	      isLimit' := ⟨evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits _ fun c => by
125	        refine IsLimit.equivOfNatIsoOfIso
126	          (cospanCompIso ((CategoryTheory.evaluation Cᵒᵖ (Type w)).obj c) f g).symm
127	          _ _ ?_ ((h c).isLimit)
128	        refine Cone.ext (Iso.refl _) ?_
129	        rintro (_ | (_ | _)) <;> cat_disch⟩ }
130	
131	/-- The open cover of a scheme attached to a family of opens with `⨆ = ⊤`. -/
132	@[simps I₀ X f]
133	noncomputable def opensCover (T : Scheme.{0}) {κ : Type} (W : κ → T.Opens)
134	    (hW : ⨆ k, W k = ⊤) : T.OpenCover where
135	  I₀ := κ
136	  X k := (W k).toScheme
137	  f k := (W k).ι
138	  mem₀ := by
139	    rw [presieve₀_mem_precoverage_iff]
140	    refine ⟨fun x => ?_, inferInstance⟩
141	    have : x ∈ ⨆ k, W k := by rw [hW]; trivial
142	    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mp this
143	    exact ⟨k, ⟨x, hk⟩, rfl⟩

145	namespace ZariskiDescent
146	
147	variable {S : Scheme.{0}} {F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1}
148	  {ι : Type} {U : ι → S.Opens}
149	
150	/-! ## §3. Glued points: the small total functor
151	
152	A *glued point* of the would-be total space over `T : Scheme` is a base
153	morphism `a : T ⟶ S` together with classifying morphisms
154	`γ i : T|_{a⁻¹ U i} ⟶ Y i` over each `U i`, whose classified `F`-sections
155	agree on the pairwise overlaps.  Through the sheaf axiom of `F` this is
156	equivalent to a morphism `a` plus a section of `F` over `(T, a)`
157	(`totalEquiv` below), but in contrast to the latter it is a `Type 0` datum. -/
158	
159	variable (U) in
160	/-- The preimage of `U i` in the parameter scheme. -/
161	abbrev pre {T : Scheme.{0}} (a : T ⟶ S) (i : ι) : T.Opens := a ⁻¹ᵁ U i
162	
163	variable (U) in
164	/-- The restriction `T|_{a⁻¹ U i} ⟶ U i` of `a`. -/
165	noncomputable abbrev preRes {T : Scheme.{0}} (a : T ⟶ S) (i : ι) :
166	    (pre U a i).toScheme ⟶ (U i).toScheme :=
167	  a.resLE (U i) (pre U a i) le_rfl
168	
169	variable (U) in
170	/-- The comparison in `Over S` between the open restriction
171	`overRes (Over.mk a) (a⁻¹ U i)` and the image under `Over.map (U i).ι` of the
172	`Over (U i)`-object `Over.mk (a.resLE …)`: the identity on total spaces. -/
173	noncomputable def classifyHom {T : Scheme.{0}} (a : T ⟶ S) (i : ι) :
174	    overRes (Over.mk a) (pre U a i) ⟶
175	      (Over.map (U i).ι).obj (Over.mk (preRes U a i)) :=
176	  Over.homMk (𝟙 (pre U a i).toScheme)
177	    (by simp only [overRes, Over.mk_hom, Over.map_obj_hom]
178	        exact Scheme.Hom.resLE_comp_ι _ _)

6	import Mathlib

8	/-!
9	# Universal global sections of a proper geometrically integral curve (campaign `B0`)
10	
11	This file supplies the **field of constants** substrate for the FGA Picard-scheme
12	representability campaign (`instHasPicScheme`, milestone `B0` of
13	`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`).
14	
15	For a curve `C` over a field `k` that is **proper** and **geometrically integral**,
16	the ring of global sections `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is:
17	
18	* a **field** (`isField_globalSections`, Stacks `0BUG`(1); Mathlib
19	  `isField_of_universallyClosed`), because a proper morphism is universally closed
20	  and `C` is integral;
21	* **finite-dimensional** over `k` (`finiteDimensional_globalSections`; Mathlib
22	  `finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), because a proper morphism is locally of
23	  finite type — so `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is a *finite field extension* of `k`.
24	
25	The sharp statement that this finite field extension is **trivial** — i.e.
26	`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` — is the content Kleiman/Milne use to build canonical divisors and
27	rigidified representatives (campaign `B1`, `B3`-corollary, `B6`, `J1`, `G3`).  Over
28	`k` it is equivalent to `k` being the *field of constants* of `C`.  We isolate the
29	content in the `Prop`-class `HasTrivialConstants` and prove the `k`-algebra
30	isomorphism `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k` from it (`globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`).
31	
32	**`HasTrivialConstants` is now UNCONDITIONAL** (`instHasTrivialConstants`, this file):
33	the honest input — degree-zero H⁰ flat base change `Γ(C_{k̄}, 𝒪) ≅ k̄ ⊗_k Γ(C, 𝒪)` —
34	is already provided by Mathlib v4.31 as the qcqs `pushoutSection` engine
35	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`, `Morphisms/Flat.lean`).
36	Over the field base the base-change morphism `Spec k̄ → Spec k` is automatically flat
37	and `C` is qcqs (proper), so base change to the algebraically closed `k̄` (where
38	`Γ(C_{k̄}, 𝒪) = k̄`, `instHasTrivialConstants_of_isAlgClosed`) plus a `finrank` count
39	forces `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`.  Consequently `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase` is now
40	**unconditional** (the `[HasTrivialConstants C]` binder auto-synthesises from
41	`[IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`).
42	
43	Campaign reference: milestone `B0` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`
44	(Part V wave landing; Kleiman §2 uses `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` implicitly throughout the
45	rigidification of `Pic^♯`).

50	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

56	/-! ## The `k`-algebra structure on the global sections `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` -/
57	
58	/-- The structural ring map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` of a `k`-curve `C`, obtained from the
59	structure morphism `C.hom : C ⟶ Spec k` on global sections, transported across
60	`Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ k`. -/
61	noncomputable def constMap (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
62	    CommRingCat.of k ⟶ Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
63	  (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ C.hom.appTop

26	`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` — is the content Kleiman/Milne use to build canonical divisors and
27	rigidified representatives (campaign `B1`, `B3`-corollary, `B6`, `J1`, `G3`).  Over
28	`k` it is equivalent to `k` being the *field of constants* of `C`.  We isolate the
29	content in the `Prop`-class `HasTrivialConstants` and prove the `k`-algebra
30	isomorphism `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k` from it (`globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`).
31	
32	**`HasTrivialConstants` is now UNCONDITIONAL** (`instHasTrivialConstants`, this file):
33	the honest input — degree-zero H⁰ flat base change `Γ(C_{k̄}, 𝒪) ≅ k̄ ⊗_k Γ(C, 𝒪)` —
34	is already provided by Mathlib v4.31 as the qcqs `pushoutSection` engine
35	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`, `Morphisms/Flat.lean`).
36	Over the field base the base-change morphism `Spec k̄ → Spec k` is automatically flat
37	and `C` is qcqs (proper), so base change to the algebraically closed `k̄` (where
38	`Γ(C_{k̄}, 𝒪) = k̄`, `instHasTrivialConstants_of_isAlgClosed`) plus a `finrank` count
39	forces `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`.  Consequently `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase` is now
40	**unconditional** (the `[HasTrivialConstants C]` binder auto-synthesises from
41	`[IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`).
42	
43	Campaign reference: milestone `B0` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`
44	(Part V wave landing; Kleiman §2 uses `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` implicitly throughout the
45	rigidification of `Pic^♯`).
46	-/

56	/-! ## The `k`-algebra structure on the global sections `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` -/
57	
58	/-- The structural ring map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` of a `k`-curve `C`, obtained from the
59	structure morphism `C.hom : C ⟶ Spec k` on global sections, transported across
60	`Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ k`. -/
61	noncomputable def constMap (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
62	    CommRingCat.of k ⟶ Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
63	  (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ C.hom.appTop
64	
65	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` induced by the structure morphism. -/
66	noncomputable scoped instance globalSectionsAlgebra (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
67	    Algebra k Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
68	  (constMap C).hom.toAlgebra

70	lemma algebraMap_globalSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
71	    algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤) = (constMap C).hom := rfl

73	/-! ## `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite field extension of `k` -/
74	
75	/-- `C` proper + geometrically integral over the one-point base `Spec k` is an
76	integral scheme. -/
77	instance isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyIntegral (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
78	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : IsIntegral C.left := by
79	  haveI : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
80	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum k))
81	  haveI : IsIntegral (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
82	    haveI : IsDomain ↑(CommRingCat.of k) := inferInstanceAs (IsDomain k)
83	    inferInstance
84	  exact GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton C.hom

86	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is a field.**  For a proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`,
87	the ring of global sections is a field (Stacks `0BUG`; Mathlib
88	`isField_of_universallyClosed`, valid because proper ⟹ universally closed and `C`
89	is integral). -/
90	theorem isField_globalSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
91	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
92	    IsField Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
93	  isField_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
94	
95	/-- The structure map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is module-finite (Mathlib
96	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`, valid because proper ⟹ locally of finite
97	type).  `constMap C = (ΓSpecIso).inv ≫ appTop` and both factors are finite (the
98	first is an isomorphism). -/
99	theorem finite_constMap (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
100	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
101	    (constMap C).hom.Finite := by
102	  have hf : (C.hom.appTop.hom).Finite :=
103	    AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
104	  have hbij := ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv
105	  have hiso : ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom).Finite :=
106	    RingHom.Finite.of_surjective _ hbij.2
107	  have hcomp : (constMap C).hom
108	      = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
109	    simp [constMap]
110	  rw [hcomp]; exact hf.comp hiso
111	
112	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is finite-dimensional over `k`.**  Combined with
113	`isField_globalSections`, this exhibits `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` as a *finite field extension*
114	of `k`. -/
115	theorem finiteDimensional_globalSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
116	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
117	    Module.Finite k Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
118	  finite_constMap C
119	
120	/-! ## `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` under the field-of-constants gate -/
121	
122	/-- **Field-of-constants gate** (`B0`).  The structure map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)`
123	is surjective — equivalently, `k` is the field of constants of `C`.  Together with
124	`isField_globalSections` this is `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`.
125	
126	The global instance `instHasTrivialConstants` (below) discharges this
127	**unconditionally** for proper geometrically integral `C/k`, via H⁰ flat base change
128	to `k̄`.  The class is kept as the reusable interface (mirroring `IsConstantField`),
129	and for the geometric semantics: `C_{k̄}` integral (geometric integrality) forces the
130	finite extension `Γ(C, 𝒪)/k` to be both separable — from geometric reducedness — and
131	to remain a domain after `⊗ k̄` — from geometric irreducibility — hence trivial. -/
132	class HasTrivialConstants (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) : Prop where
133	  surjective_constMap : Function.Surjective (constMap C).hom
134	
135	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k`.**  Under the field-of-constants gate, the finite field
136	extension `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)/k` is trivial: the structure map is a `k`-algebra
137	isomorphism.  (Injectivity is automatic — `k` is a field and `Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is
138	nonzero.) -/
139	noncomputable def globalSectionsAlgEquivBase (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
140	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasTrivialConstants C] :
141	    Γ(C.left, ⊤) ≃ₐ[k] k := by
142	  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(C.left, ⊤) := (isField_globalSections C).nontrivial
143	  have hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤)) :=
144	    (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤)).injective
145	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤)) :=
146	    HasTrivialConstants.surjective_constMap
147	  exact (AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId k Γ(C.left, ⊤)) ⟨hinj, hsurj⟩).symm
148	
149	/-- **The field-of-constants gate is unconditional over an algebraically closed
150	base.**  A finite field extension of an algebraically closed field is trivial, so
151	`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` needs no extra hypothesis when `k = k̄`
152	(`IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`).  This discharges
153	`HasTrivialConstants` in the geometric case `C_{k̄}` that the Milne route reduces
154	to (campaign `J`-cluster works over separably/algebraically closed `k'`). -/
155	instance instHasTrivialConstants_of_isAlgClosed (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
156	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [IsAlgClosed k] :
157	    HasTrivialConstants C := by
158	  letI : Field Γ(C.left, ⊤) := (isField_globalSections C).toField
159	  haveI : Module.Finite k Γ(C.left, ⊤) := finiteDimensional_globalSections C
160	  haveI : Algebra.IsIntegral k Γ(C.left, ⊤) := Algebra.IsIntegral.of_finite k _
161	  exact ⟨(IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral (k := k)
162	    (K := Γ(C.left, ⊤))).2⟩

164	/-! ## `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` unconditionally, via H⁰ flat base change
165	
166	The field-of-constants gate `HasTrivialConstants` is discharged **unconditionally** for a
167	proper geometrically integral curve `C/k` by base change to an algebraically closed
168	extension `K/k` (e.g. `K = k̄`) together with Mathlib's qcqs `H⁰` flat base-change engine
169	`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right` (`Morphisms/Flat.lean`):
170	
171	* the base-change morphism `Spec K → Spec k` is automatically flat (the base `Spec k` is a
172	  subsingleton integral scheme), and `C` is qcqs (proper), so the canonical map
173	  `Γ(Spec K, 𝒪) ⊗_{Γ(Spec k,𝒪)} Γ(C, 𝒪) → Γ(C_K, 𝒪)` is an isomorphism;
174	* over the algebraically closed `K`, `Γ(C_K, 𝒪) = K` (the already-available
175	  `instHasTrivialConstants_of_isAlgClosed`), so a `finrank` count over `Γ(Spec K, 𝒪)`
176	  forces `Γ(Spec k, 𝒪) → Γ(C, 𝒪)` to be an isomorphism, i.e. `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k`.
177	
178	This is the campaign `B0`/wave-1 degree-zero H⁰ flat base-change brick (reused across `B2`,
179	`B3`, `B4`, `B5`, `D2'`); see `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md` Part III `C3`. -/

182	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
183	/-- **H⁰ flat base change over a field base (structure sheaf).**  For a qcqs `k`-scheme `X`
184	(e.g. proper) and **any** `k`-algebra `A`, the canonical base-change map is a
185	`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪)`-algebra isomorphism
186	`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) ⊗_{Γ(Spec k,𝒪)} Γ(X, 𝒪) ≅ Γ(X ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)`.
187	
188	Over the field base `Spec k` the base-change morphism `Spec A → Spec k` is automatically flat
189	(`Spec k` is subsingleton integral), so Mathlib's qcqs `pushoutSection` engine
190	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) applies; the `≃ₐ` is assembled from
191	`CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct` exactly as `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Normalization.lean`.
192	The three source-ring `Algebra` instances (non-canonical — they come from the `appTop`/`appLE`
193	section maps) are supplied via `letI` in the return type.  Campaign `B0`/wave-1 item (iv). -/
194	noncomputable def globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv
195	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (iX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
196	    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
197	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
198	    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) :=
199	      ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
200	    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(X, ⊤) := (iX.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
201	    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
202	        ↥Γ(pullback iX (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))), ⊤) :=
203	      ((pullback.snd iX (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
204	    ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) ⊗[↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)] ↥Γ(X, ⊤)
205	      ≃ₐ[↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)]
206	      ↥Γ(pullback iX (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))), ⊤) := by
207	  let g : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
208	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
209	  have hU : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).Opens) := isAffineOpen_top _
210	  have hV : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens) := isAffineOpen_top _
211	  have hthis := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
212	    (.of_hasPullback iX g) (le_top) (le_refl _) (UY := pullback.snd iX g ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)
213	    (by simp) hU hV (iX.isCompact_preimage hU.isCompact)
214	    (iX.isQuasiSeparated_preimage hU.isQuasiSeparated)
215	  algebraize [(iX.appTop).hom, (g.appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom,
216	    ((pullback.snd iX g).appTop).hom]
217	  let e₀ := (CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct
218	      (↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)) (↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤))
219	      (↥Γ(X, ⊤))).flip.isoPushout ≪≫
220	    (pushout.congrHom iX.app_eq_appLE rfl ≪≫ @asIso _ _ _ _ _ hthis :)
221	  exact
222	    { toRingEquiv := e₀.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
223	      commutes' := fun r => by
224	        change (CommRingCat.ofHom Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom ≫ e₀.hom) r =
225	          ((pullback.snd iX g).app ⊤) r
226	        congr 2
227	        simp [e₀, pushout.inr_desc_assoc, Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE] }
228	
229	open TensorProduct Limits in
230	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
231	/-- **Surjectivity of the field-of-constants map via base change to an algebraically closed
232	extension.**  For a proper geometrically integral curve `C/k` and any algebraically closed
233	field extension `K/k`, the structure map `k → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` is surjective.  Proof: H⁰ flat base
234	change gives `Γ(Spec K, 𝒪) ⊗_{Γ(Spec k,𝒪)} Γ(C, 𝒪) ≅ Γ(C_K, 𝒪)`, and `Γ(C_K, 𝒪) = K` over
235	the algebraically closed `K` forces the `Γ(Spec k,𝒪)`-dimension of `Γ(C, 𝒪)` to be `1`. -/
236	theorem surjective_constMap_of_isAlgClosed_baseChange
237	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
238	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
239	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsAlgClosed K] :
240	    Function.Surjective (constMap C).hom := by
241	  classical
242	  let g : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
243	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))
244	  haveI hpq : IsProper (pullback.snd C.hom g) := inferInstance
245	  haveI hgiq : GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.snd C.hom g) := inferInstance
246	  haveI : IsProper (Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom g)).hom := hpq
247	  haveI : GeometricallyIntegral (Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom g)).hom := hgiq
248	  have hVU : (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).Opens) ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := le_top
249	  have hU : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).Opens) := isAffineOpen_top _
250	  have hV : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).Opens) := isAffineOpen_top _
251	  have hthis := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
252	    (.of_hasPullback C.hom g) hVU (le_refl _) (UY := pullback.snd C.hom g ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤)
253	    (by simp) hU hV (C.hom.isCompact_preimage hU.isCompact)
254	    (C.hom.isQuasiSeparated_preimage hU.isQuasiSeparated)
255	  algebraize [(C.hom.appTop).hom, (g.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hVU).hom,
256	    ((pullback.snd C.hom g).appTop).hom]
257	  let e₀ := (CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct
258	      (↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)) (↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤))
259	      (↥Γ(C.left, ⊤))).flip.isoPushout ≪≫
260	    (pushout.congrHom C.hom.app_eq_appLE rfl ≪≫ @asIso _ _ _ _ _ hthis :)
261	  let e : Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) ⊗[Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)] Γ(C.left, ⊤)
262	      ≃ₐ[Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤)] Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤) :=
263	    { toRingEquiv := e₀.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
264	      commutes' := fun r => by
265	        change (CommRingCat.ofHom Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom ≫ e₀.hom) r =
266	          ((pullback.snd C.hom g).app ⊤) r
267	        congr 2
268	        simp [e₀, pushout.inr_desc_assoc, Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE] }
269	  -- The section rings of the affine bases `Spec k`, `Spec K` are fields.
270	  letI : Field ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) :=
271	    (MulEquiv.isField (Field.toIsField k)
272	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv).toField
273	  letI : Field ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
274	    (MulEquiv.isField (Field.toIsField K)
275	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv).toField
276	  -- `Γ(C_K, 𝒪)` is a field and `Γ(Spec K,𝒪) → Γ(C_K,𝒪)` is bijective (`K` alg. closed).
277	  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤) :=
278	    (isField_globalSections (k := K) (Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom g))).nontrivial
279	  have hsurjK : Function.Surjective ⇑((pullback.snd C.hom g).appTop).hom := by
280	    have hh := (instHasTrivialConstants_of_isAlgClosed (k := K)
281	      (Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom g))).surjective_constMap
282	    rw [show constMap (Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom g))
283	        = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ (pullback.snd C.hom g).appTop from rfl,
284	      CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.coe_comp] at hh
285	    exact hh.of_comp
286	  have hM1 : Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤) = 1 := by
287	    rw [Algebra.finrank_eq_one_iff_bijective_algebraMap]
288	    exact ⟨(algebraMap ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤)
289	      ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤)).injective, hsurjK⟩
290	  -- Transport the finrank through base change and the iso `e`.
291	  have hbc : Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤)
292	      (↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) ⊗[↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)] ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤))
293	      = Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
294	    Module.finrank_baseChange
295	  have he : Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤)
296	      (↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) ⊗[↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)] ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤))
297	      = Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤) :=
298	    e.toLinearEquiv.finrank_eq
299	  have hL1 : Module.finrank ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) = 1 := by
300	    rw [← hbc, he, hM1]
301	  rw [Algebra.finrank_eq_one_iff_bijective_algebraMap] at hL1
302	  -- Conclude: `constMap C = ΓSpecIso.inv ≫ C.hom.appTop` is surjective.
303	  have hbij : Function.Bijective ⇑(C.hom.appTop).hom := hL1
304	  change Function.Surjective
305	    ⇑((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ C.hom.appTop).hom
306	  rw [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.coe_comp]
307	  exact hbij.surjective.comp
308	    (ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv).surjective
309	
310	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` unconditionally** — the field-of-constants gate `HasTrivialConstants`
311	is discharged for every proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, with no
312	algebraic-closedness or rational-point hypothesis, via H⁰ flat base change to `k̄`
313	(`surjective_constMap_of_isAlgClosed_baseChange` with `K = AlgebraicClosure k`).  This closes
314	the campaign `B0` residual, making `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase : Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₐ[k] k`
315	unconditional. -/
316	instance instHasTrivialConstants (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
317	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasTrivialConstants C :=
318	  ⟨surjective_constMap_of_isAlgClosed_baseChange C (AlgebraicClosure k)⟩
319	
320	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-- The structure map `Γ(Spec k, 𝒪) → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` of a proper geometrically integral
curve `C/k` is bijective (field of constants: `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`). -/
theorem bijective_hom_appTop (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    Function.Bijective (C.hom.appTop).hom := by
  have hconst : Function.Bijective (constMap C).hom := by
    have := globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C
    constructor
    · exact (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤)).injective
    · exact HasTrivialConstants.surjective_constMap
  have hiso : Function.Bijective (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom :=
    ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso _
  have hcomp : (constMap C).hom
      = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
    simp [constMap]
  rw [hcomp] at hconst
  exact (Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff _ hiso).mp hconst

/-! ## `lm:aut`: global functions on `C × T` are pulled back from `T`, uniquely

The ring-theoretic heart of the automorphism-rigidity lemma (Kleiman §2, rigidification of
`Pic^♯`): if the structure map `f : Γ(T, 𝒪) → Γ(C × T, 𝒪)` is bijective (P1/P2) and admits a
retraction `s` coming from a section `σ : T ⟶ C × T` of `π`, then every global function on
`C × T` is `f` of its restriction along `σ`.  Stated abstractly on rings so it is reusable for
both the affine base (P1) and the general base (P2). -/

/-- **Pulled-back-from-`T` (ring form).**  If `f : R →+* S` is bijective with retraction
`s : S →+* R` (`s ∘ f = id`), then every `u : S` satisfies `f (s u) = u`: `u` is determined by
its restriction `s u`.  Here `f = π.appTop` (the structure-sheaf comparison map) and `s = σ.appTop`
for a section `σ` of `π`. -/
theorem eq_apply_of_isRetraction {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (s : S →+* R) (hf : Function.Bijective f)
    (hsf : s.comp f = RingHom.id R) (u : S) : f (s u) = u := by
  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hf.surjective u
  rw [← RingHom.comp_apply, hsf, RingHom.id_apply]

/-- **Automorphism rigidity (ring form, `lm:aut`).**  A global function `u` on `C × T` whose
restriction along the section `σ` is `1` (`s u = 1`) is itself `1`, provided the comparison map
`f = π.appTop` is bijective and `s = σ.appTop` retracts it.  Downstream: a unit on `C × T`
rigidified to `1` along `σ` equals `1`. -/
theorem eq_one_of_isRetraction_of_restrict_eq_one {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (s : S →+* R) (hf : Function.Bijective f)
    (hsf : s.comp f = RingHom.id R) (u : S) (hu : s u = 1) : u = 1 := by
  have h := eq_apply_of_isRetraction f s hf hsf u
  rw [hu, map_one] at h
  exact h.symm

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-- **Global functions on `C × T` are pulled back from `T`, uniquely (scheme form).**  Given the
field-of-constants comparison bijectivity `hbij` (P1 for `T = Spec A`, P2 for general `T`) and a
section `σ` of `π = pullback.snd C.hom πT`, every global function `u` on `C × T` equals the
pullback along `π` of its restriction `σ.appTop u` along the section. -/
theorem appTop_restrict_eq_of_section (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (hbij : Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom)
    (σ : T ⟶ pullback C.hom πT) (hσ : σ ≫ pullback.snd C.hom πT = 𝟙 T)
    (u : ↥Γ(pullback C.hom πT, ⊤)) :
    ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom ((σ.appTop).hom u) = u :=
  eq_apply_of_isRetraction _ _ hbij (retraction_appTop_of_section C πT σ hσ) u

/-- **Automorphism rigidity for `C × T` (`lm:aut`, scheme form).**  Given the field-of-constants
comparison bijectivity `hbij` and a section `σ` of `π`, any global function `u` on `C × T` whose
restriction along `σ` is `1` equals `1` (Kleiman §2 rigidification of `Pic^♯`: a unit rigidified
to `1` along the identity section is trivial). -/
theorem eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (hbij : Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom)
    (σ : T ⟶ pullback C.hom πT) (hσ : σ ≫ pullback.snd C.hom πT = 𝟙 T)
    (u : ↥Γ(pullback C.hom πT, ⊤)) (hu : (σ.appTop).hom u = 1) : u = 1 :=
  eq_one_of_isRetraction_of_restrict_eq_one _ _ hbij
    (retraction_appTop_of_section C πT σ hσ) u hu

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-! ## P2: the sheaf-level H⁰ base-change brick over an arbitrary base `T`

For an arbitrary `k`-scheme `T` with structure morphism `πT : T ⟶ Spec k`, the structure-sheaf
comparison `𝒪_T ⟶ π_* 𝒪_{C×T}` (`π = pullback.snd C.hom πT`) is an isomorphism.  The proof route
(Kleiman §2; cohomology-and-base-change in degree `0`) is: for every affine open `V ⊆ T` the
restricted comparison `Γ(T, V) → Γ(C × T, π⁻¹V)` is the P1 base-change iso at `A = Γ(V, 𝒪)`
(because `π⁻¹V ≅ C ×_k V`), and these per-affine-open isos assemble to a sheaf isomorphism on the
affine-opens basis `T.isBasis_affineOpens` via stalks (mirroring
`QuotScheme.isIso_sheaf_of_isIso_app_basicOpen`).

The AFFINE base case `T = Spec A` is UNCONDITIONAL (it is exactly P1,
`isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange`).  For a general base the per-affine-open identification of `π⁻¹V`
with the base change `C ×_k V` plus the stalk assembly is packaged behind the `Prop`-class
`HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso` below (there is NO sorried instance — the class is discharged
unconditionally only in the affine case, where P1 supplies it).  Every downstream consumer (`lm:aut`)
is proved *modulo this gate*, and instantiated unconditionally for affine `T`. -/

/-- **Gate (`B1`, P2): the structure-sheaf pushforward comparison is an isomorphism.**  Carries the
conclusion `IsIso (π.appTop)` — equivalently `Γ(T, 𝒪) → Γ(C × T, 𝒪)` bijective — for the second
projection `π = pullback.snd C.hom πT` of the relative product.

Unconditional for affine `T = Spec A` (`instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_baseChange`, from P1).
For a general base it encapsulates the (Mathlib-absent) per-affine-open + stalk assembly of the
degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change theorem; it is kept as the reusable interface so the
automorphism-rigidity consumers of campaign `B1` are available for every `T` that supplies it. -/
class HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) : Prop where
  isIso_appTop : IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop)

/-- **The gate is unconditional for an affine base** (it *is* P1).  For `T = Spec A` the comparison
`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` is the P1 base-change isomorphism. -/
instance instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_baseChange (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
    HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso C (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) :=
  ⟨isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange C A⟩

/-- Extract the global-sections bijectivity from the gate. -/
theorem bijective_appTop_of_hasStructureSheafPushforwardIso
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso C πT] :
    Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom :=
  (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mp HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso.isIso_appTop

/-!
# Sheaf-level H⁰ base change for a proper geometrically integral curve (campaign `B1`)

For a proper geometrically integral curve `C` over a field `k` and an arbitrary `k`-scheme `T`
(`πT : T ⟶ Spec k`), let `π := pullback.snd C.hom πT : (C ×_k T) ⟶ T` be the second projection of
the relative product.  The structure-sheaf pushforward comparison `𝒪_T ⟶ π_* 𝒪_{C ×_k T}` is an
**isomorphism**: a global function on `C ×_k T` is pulled back from `T`.  Geometrically this is the
degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change statement `Γ(C_κ, 𝒪) = κ` on every fibre (the field of
constants, campaign `B0`), and its commutation with base change.

This file supplies the `B1` brick and its automorphism-freeness consumer (Kleiman §2,
rigidification of `Pic^♯`).  Contents:

* **P1 — affine base** (unconditional): `bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange` /
  `isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange`: for `A` a `k`-algebra, `Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` is
  bijective.  Proof: the `B0` base-change isomorphism
  `Γ(Spec A) ⊗_{Γ(Spec k)} Γ(C) ≅ Γ(C ×_k Spec A)` (`globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv`) composed
  with `includeLeft`, which is bijective because the right tensor factor `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` collapses
  (`Γ(C, 𝒪) ≃ₐ[k] k`, `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`).  Generalised to **any affine base scheme**
  `W` with any `πT : W ⟶ Spec k` in `bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine` (transport across
  `W ≅ Spec Γ(W, 𝒪)`).

* **P2 — arbitrary base** (`HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso`): the sheaf-level iso `IsIso π.appTop`
  for a general `T`.  Discharged **unconditionally for every affine `T`**
  (`instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_of_isAffine`, from P1); for a general base it is kept as a
  `Prop`-class gate (there is **no sorried instance**) encapsulating the per-affine-open + stalk
  assembly of the degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change theorem, which mirrors
  `QuotScheme.isIso_sheaf_of_isIso_app_basicOpen` on the affine-opens basis `T.isBasis_affineOpens`
  but is not carried out here.  All P3 consumers are proved *modulo the gate* and instantiated
  unconditionally for affine `T`.

* **P3 — `lm:aut`** (unconditional at the ring level): `eq_apply_of_isRetraction` /
  `eq_one_of_isRetraction_of_restrict_eq_one` (ring form) and their scheme wrappers
  `appTop_restrict_eq_of_section`, `eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one`(`_of_gate`): a section
  `σ` of `π` retracts the (bijective) comparison map, so a global function on `C ×_k T` rigidified
  to `1` along `σ` equals `1`.

Campaign reference: milestone `B1` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`; Kleiman §2.
Substrate: `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean` (campaign `B0`).
-/

9	/-!
10	# Sheaf-level H⁰ base change for a proper geometrically integral curve (campaign `B1`)
11	
12	For a proper geometrically integral curve `C` over a field `k` and an arbitrary `k`-scheme `T`
13	(`πT : T ⟶ Spec k`), let `π := pullback.snd C.hom πT : (C ×_k T) ⟶ T` be the second projection of
14	the relative product.  The structure-sheaf pushforward comparison `𝒪_T ⟶ π_* 𝒪_{C ×_k T}` is an
15	**isomorphism**: a global function on `C ×_k T` is pulled back from `T`.  Geometrically this is the
16	degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change statement `Γ(C_κ, 𝒪) = κ` on every fibre (the field of
17	constants, campaign `B0`), and its commutation with base change.
18	
19	This file supplies the `B1` brick and its automorphism-freeness consumer (Kleiman §2,
20	rigidification of `Pic^♯`).  Contents:
21	
22	* **P1 — affine base** (unconditional): `bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange` /
23	  `isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange`: for `A` a `k`-algebra, `Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` is
24	  bijective.  Proof: the `B0` base-change isomorphism
25	  `Γ(Spec A) ⊗_{Γ(Spec k)} Γ(C) ≅ Γ(C ×_k Spec A)` (`globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv`) composed
26	  with `includeLeft`, which is bijective because the right tensor factor `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` collapses
27	  (`Γ(C, 𝒪) ≃ₐ[k] k`, `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`).  Generalised to **any affine base scheme**
28	  `W` with any `πT : W ⟶ Spec k` in `bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine` (transport across
29	  `W ≅ Spec Γ(W, 𝒪)`).
30	
31	* **P2 — arbitrary base** (`HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso`): the sheaf-level iso `IsIso π.appTop`
32	  for a general `T`.  Discharged **unconditionally for every affine `T`**
33	  (`instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_of_isAffine`, from P1); for a general base it is kept as a
34	  `Prop`-class gate (there is **no sorried instance**) encapsulating the per-affine-open + stalk

36	  `QuotScheme.isIso_sheaf_of_isIso_app_basicOpen` on the affine-opens basis `T.isBasis_affineOpens`

43	  `σ` of `π` retracts the (bijective) comparison map, so a global function on `C ×_k T` rigidified

61	curve `C/k` is bijective (field of constants: `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`). -/
62	theorem bijective_hom_appTop (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
63	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
64	    Function.Bijective (C.hom.appTop).hom := by
65	  have hconst : Function.Bijective (constMap C).hom := by
66	    have := globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C
67	    constructor

69	    · exact HasTrivialConstants.surjective_constMap

71	    ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso _
72	  have hcomp : (constMap C).hom
73	      = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
74	    simp [constMap]
75	  rw [hcomp] at hconst
76	  exact (Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff _ hiso).mp hconst

82	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
83	    Function.Bijective
84	      ((pullback.snd C.hom
85	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).appTop).hom := by
86	  set g : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
87	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) with hg
88	  letI instSA : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) :=

92	  letI instPull : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
93	      ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤) :=
94	    ((pullback.snd C.hom g).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
95	  haveI : CompactSpace C.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace C.hom
96	  haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace C.left := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated C.hom
97	  have e := globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv C.hom A
98	  -- The structure map `R = Γ(Spec k) → M = Γ(C)` is bijective (field of constants),
99	  -- so `M ≃ₐ[R] R`, hence `S ⊗[R] M ≃ₐ[S] S`, hence `includeLeft = algebraMap S (S⊗M)`
100	  -- is bijective; composing with the base-change iso `e` gives the claim.
101	  set R := ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
102	  set S := ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
103	  set M := ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤)

105	  let φ : M ≃ₐ[R] R := (AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId R M) hRM).symm
106	  let ε : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₐ[S] S :=
107	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr AlgEquiv.refl φ).trans (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid R S S)

110	    have h := ε.commutes s
111	    simp only [Algebra.algebraMap_self, RingHom.id_apply] at h
112	    exact ε.eq_symm_apply.mpr h

114	    have : ⇑(algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] M)) = ⇑ε.symm := funext hb2
115	    rw [this]; exact ε.symm.bijective
116	  change Function.Bijective ⇑(algebraMap S ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤))
117	  have hcomp : ⇑(algebraMap S ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤))
118	      = ⇑e ∘ ⇑(algebraMap S (S ⊗[R] M)) := by
119	    funext s; exact (e.commutes s).symm
120	  rw [hcomp]
121	  exact e.bijective.comp hleft
122	
123	/-- **P1 as an isomorphism of `CommRingCat` objects.**  The comparison ring map
124	`Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` is an isomorphism. -/
125	theorem isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
126	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
127	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
128	    IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom
129	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).appTop) :=
130	  (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr (bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange C A)
131	
132	/-- `appTop` of an isomorphism is an isomorphism (`appTop` is contravariantly functorial). -/
133	private lemma isIso_appTop_of_isIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] :
134	    IsIso (f.appTop) := by
135	  refine ⟨(inv f).appTop, ?_, ?_⟩
136	  · rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, IsIso.inv_hom_id]; simp
137	  · rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, IsIso.hom_inv_id]; simp
138	
139	/-- **P1 for an arbitrary affine base scheme.**  For any affine scheme `W` and any structure
140	morphism `h : W ⟶ Spec k`, the comparison `Γ(W, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k W, 𝒪)` is bijective.  This is P1
141	transported across `W ≅ Spec Γ(W, 𝒪)` (every affine `W` is `Spec` of its global sections, and every
142	`Spec Γ(W) ⟶ Spec k` is `Spec.map` of a ring map, i.e. gives `Γ(W)` a `k`-algebra structure). -/
143	theorem bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
144	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
145	    {W : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine W] (h : W ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :
146	    Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom h).appTop).hom := by
147	  set e : W ≅ Spec Γ(W, ⊤) := W.isoSpec with he
148	  set h₀ : Spec Γ(W, ⊤) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) := e.inv ≫ h with hh0
149	  have hh : h = e.hom ≫ h₀ := by rw [hh0, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]

153	  have hP1 := bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange C Γ(W, ⊤)

155	    rw [show (algebraMap k Γ(W, ⊤)) = CommRingCat.Hom.hom φ from rfl,
156	      CommRingCat.ofHom_hom, hspec]
157	  rw [hbase] at hP1
158	  -- Transport across the arrow isomorphism `m` (base change along `e.hom : W ≅ Spec Γ(W)`).

169	  haveI : IsIso (e.hom.appTop) := isIso_appTop_of_isIso e.hom

172	        = inv (e.hom.appTop) ≫ (pullback.snd C.hom h₀).appTop ≫ m.appTop := by
173	      rw [key, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc]

202	class HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
203	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) : Prop where
204	  isIso_appTop : IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop)

207	`T` and any structure map `πT : T ⟶ Spec k`, the comparison `Γ(T, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k T, 𝒪)` is the
208	(transported) P1 base-change isomorphism (`bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine`).  In particular it
209	fires for `T = Spec A` and for the affine chart `V.toScheme` of any affine open `V ⊆ T`. -/
210	instance instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_of_isAffine (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

212	    {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :
213	    HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso C πT :=

224

226	`Pic^♯`): if the structure map `f : Γ(T, 𝒪) → Γ(C × T, 𝒪)` is bijective (P1/P2) and admits a

variable [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback f' (pullback.fst f g)]

instance hasPullbackHorizPaste : HasPullback (f' ≫ f) g :=
  HasLimit.mk {
    cone := (pullback.cone f g).pasteHoriz (pullback.cone f' (pullback.fst f g)) rfl
    isLimit := pasteHorizIsPullback rfl (pullback.isLimit f g)
      (pullback.isLimit f' (pullback.fst f g))
  }

/-- The canonical isomorphism `W ×[X] (X ×[Z] Y) ≅ W ×[Z] Y` -/
noncomputable def pullbackRightPullbackFstIso :
    pullback f' (pullback.fst f g) ≅ pullback (f' ≫ f) g :=
  IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso
    (pasteHorizIsPullback rfl (pullback.isLimit f g) (pullback.isLimit f' (pullback.fst f g)))
    (pullback.isLimit (f' ≫ f) g)

6	import Mathlib

9	/-!
10	# Sheaf-level H⁰ base change for a proper geometrically integral curve (campaign `B1`)
11	
12	For a proper geometrically integral curve `C` over a field `k` and an arbitrary `k`-scheme `T`
13	(`πT : T ⟶ Spec k`), let `π := pullback.snd C.hom πT : (C ×_k T) ⟶ T` be the second projection of
14	the relative product.  The structure-sheaf pushforward comparison `𝒪_T ⟶ π_* 𝒪_{C ×_k T}` is an
15	**isomorphism**: a global function on `C ×_k T` is pulled back from `T`.  Geometrically this is the
16	degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change statement `Γ(C_κ, 𝒪) = κ` on every fibre (the field of
17	constants, campaign `B0`), and its commutation with base change.
18	
19	This file supplies the `B1` brick and its automorphism-freeness consumer (Kleiman §2,
20	rigidification of `Pic^♯`).  Contents:
21	
22	* **P1 — affine base** (unconditional): `bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange` /
23	  `isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange`: for `A` a `k`-algebra, `Γ(Spec A, 𝒪) → Γ(C ×_k Spec A, 𝒪)` is
24	  bijective.  Proof: the `B0` base-change isomorphism
25	  `Γ(Spec A) ⊗_{Γ(Spec k)} Γ(C) ≅ Γ(C ×_k Spec A)` (`globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv`) composed
26	  with `includeLeft`, which is bijective because the right tensor factor `Γ(C, 𝒪) = k` collapses
27	  (`Γ(C, 𝒪) ≃ₐ[k] k`, `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`).  Generalised to **any affine base scheme**
28	  `W` with any `πT : W ⟶ Spec k` in `bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine` (transport across
29	  `W ≅ Spec Γ(W, 𝒪)`).
30	
31	* **P2 — arbitrary base** (`HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso`): the sheaf-level iso `IsIso π.appTop`
32	  for a general `T`.  Discharged **unconditionally for every affine `T`**
33	  (`instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_of_isAffine`, from P1); for a general base it is kept as a
34	  `Prop`-class gate (there is **no sorried instance**) encapsulating the per-affine-open + stalk
35	  assembly of the degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change theorem, which mirrors
36	  `QuotScheme.isIso_sheaf_of_isIso_app_basicOpen` on the affine-opens basis `T.isBasis_affineOpens`
37	  but is not carried out here.  All P3 consumers are proved *modulo the gate* and instantiated
38	  unconditionally for affine `T`.
39	
40	* **P3 — `lm:aut`** (unconditional at the ring level): `eq_apply_of_isRetraction` /
41	  `eq_one_of_isRetraction_of_restrict_eq_one` (ring form) and their scheme wrappers
42	  `appTop_restrict_eq_of_section`, `eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one`(`_of_gate`): a section
43	  `σ` of `π` retracts the (bijective) comparison map, so a global function on `C ×_k T` rigidified
44	  to `1` along `σ` equals `1`.
45	
46	Campaign reference: milestone `B1` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`; Kleiman §2.
47	Substrate: `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean` (campaign `B0`).

54	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry
55	
56	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
57	
58	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
59	
60	/-- The structure map `Γ(Spec k, 𝒪) → Γ(C, 𝒪_C)` of a proper geometrically integral
61	curve `C/k` is bijective (field of constants: `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k`). -/
62	theorem bijective_hom_appTop (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
63	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
64	    Function.Bijective (C.hom.appTop).hom := by
65	  have hconst : Function.Bijective (constMap C).hom := by
66	    have := globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C
67	    constructor
68	    · exact (algebraMap k Γ(C.left, ⊤)).injective
69	    · exact HasTrivialConstants.surjective_constMap
70	  have hiso : Function.Bijective (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom :=
71	    ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso _
72	  have hcomp : (constMap C).hom
73	      = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
74	    simp [constMap]
75	  rw [hcomp] at hconst
76	  exact (Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff _ hiso).mp hconst
77	
78	open TensorProduct in
79	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
80	theorem bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
81	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
82	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
83	    Function.Bijective
84	      ((pullback.snd C.hom
85	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).appTop).hom := by
86	  set g : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
87	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) with hg
88	  letI instSA : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤) :=
89	    ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom.toAlgebra
90	  letI instMA : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤) ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) :=
91	    (C.hom.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
92	  letI instPull : Algebra ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
93	      ↥Γ(pullback C.hom g, ⊤) :=
94	    ((pullback.snd C.hom g).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
95	  haveI : CompactSpace C.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace C.hom
96	  haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace C.left := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated C.hom
97	  have e := globalSectionsBaseChangeAlgEquiv C.hom A
98	  -- The structure map `R = Γ(Spec k) → M = Γ(C)` is bijective (field of constants),
99	  -- so `M ≃ₐ[R] R`, hence `S ⊗[R] M ≃ₐ[S] S`, hence `includeLeft = algebraMap S (S⊗M)`
100	  -- is bijective; composing with the base-change iso `e` gives the claim.
101	  set R := ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of k), ⊤)
102	  set S := ↥Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of A), ⊤)
103	  set M := ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤)
104	  have hRM : Function.Bijective (algebraMap R M) := bijective_hom_appTop C
105	  let φ : M ≃ₐ[R] R := (AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId R M) hRM).symm

139	/-- **P1 for an arbitrary affine base scheme.**  For any affine scheme `W` and any structure

141	transported across `W ≅ Spec Γ(W, 𝒪)` (every affine `W` is `Spec` of its global sections, and every

146	    Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom h).appTop).hom := by
147	  set e : W ≅ Spec Γ(W, ⊤) := W.isoSpec with he
148	  set h₀ : Spec Γ(W, ⊤) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) := e.inv ≫ h with hh0
149	  have hh : h = e.hom ≫ h₀ := by rw [hh0, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
150	  set φ : CommRingCat.of k ⟶ Γ(W, ⊤) := Spec.preimage h₀ with hφ
151	  have hspec : Spec.map φ = h₀ := Spec.map_preimage h₀
152	  letI : Algebra k Γ(W, ⊤) := φ.hom.toAlgebra
153	  have hP1 := bijective_snd_appTop_baseChange C Γ(W, ⊤)
154	  have hbase : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(W, ⊤))) = h₀ := by

162	  have hcompat : m ≫ pullback.snd C.hom h₀ = pullback.snd C.hom h ≫ e.hom := by

167	    (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr hP1

169	  haveI : IsIso (e.hom.appTop) := isIso_appTop_of_isIso e.hom

171	    have hh2 : (pullback.snd C.hom h).appTop
172	        = inv (e.hom.appTop) ≫ (pullback.snd C.hom h₀).appTop ≫ m.appTop := by
173	      rw [key, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc]

177	/-! ## P2: the sheaf-level H⁰ base-change brick over an arbitrary base `T`
178	
179	For an arbitrary `k`-scheme `T` with structure morphism `πT : T ⟶ Spec k`, the structure-sheaf
180	comparison `𝒪_T ⟶ π_* 𝒪_{C×T}` (`π = pullback.snd C.hom πT`) is an isomorphism.  The proof route
181	(Kleiman §2; cohomology-and-base-change in degree `0`) is: for every affine open `V ⊆ T` the
182	restricted comparison `Γ(T, V) → Γ(C × T, π⁻¹V)` is the P1 base-change iso at `A = Γ(V, 𝒪)`
183	(because `π⁻¹V ≅ C ×_k V`), and these per-affine-open isos assemble to a sheaf isomorphism on the
184	affine-opens basis `T.isBasis_affineOpens` via stalks (mirroring
185	`QuotScheme.isIso_sheaf_of_isIso_app_basicOpen`).
186	
187	The AFFINE base case `T = Spec A` is UNCONDITIONAL (it is exactly P1,
188	`isIso_snd_appTop_baseChange`).  For a general base the per-affine-open identification of `π⁻¹V`
189	with the base change `C ×_k V` plus the stalk assembly is packaged behind the `Prop`-class
190	`HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso` below (there is NO sorried instance — the class is discharged
191	unconditionally only in the affine case, where P1 supplies it).  Every downstream consumer
192	(`lm:aut`) is proved *modulo this gate*, and instantiated unconditionally for affine `T`. -/
193	
194	/-- **Gate (`B1`, P2): the structure-sheaf pushforward comparison is an isomorphism.**  Carries the
195	conclusion `IsIso (π.appTop)` — equivalently `Γ(T, 𝒪) → Γ(C × T, 𝒪)` bijective — for the second
196	projection `π = pullback.snd C.hom πT` of the relative product.
197	
198	Unconditional for any affine `T` (`instHasStructureSheafPushforwardIso_of_isAffine`, from P1).
199	For a general base it encapsulates the (Mathlib-absent) per-affine-open + stalk assembly of the
200	degree-`0` cohomology-and-base-change theorem; it is kept as the reusable interface so the
201	automorphism-rigidity consumers of campaign `B1` are available for every `T` that supplies it. -/
202	class HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
203	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) : Prop where
204	  isIso_appTop : IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop)

213	    HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso C πT :=

223	/-! ## `lm:aut`: global functions on `C × T` are pulled back from `T`, uniquely
224	
225	The ring-theoretic heart of the automorphism-rigidity lemma (Kleiman §2, rigidification of
226	`Pic^♯`): if the structure map `f : Γ(T, 𝒪) → Γ(C × T, 𝒪)` is bijective (P1/P2) and admits a
227	retraction `s` coming from a section `σ : T ⟶ C × T` of `π`, then every global function on
228	`C × T` is `f` of its restriction along `σ`.  Stated abstractly on rings so it is reusable for
229	both the affine base (P1) and the general base (P2). -/
230	
231	/-- **Pulled-back-from-`T` (ring form).**  If `f : R →+* S` is bijective with retraction
232	`s : S →+* R` (`s ∘ f = id`), then every `u : S` satisfies `f (s u) = u`: `u` is determined by
233	its restriction `s u`.  Here `f = π.appTop` (the structure-sheaf comparison map) and `s = σ.appTop`
234	for a section `σ` of `π`. -/
235	theorem eq_apply_of_isRetraction {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
236	    (f : R →+* S) (s : S →+* R) (hf : Function.Bijective f)
237	    (hsf : s.comp f = RingHom.id R) (u : S) : f (s u) = u := by
238	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hf.surjective u
239	  have hsr : s (f r) = r := by rw [← RingHom.comp_apply, hsf, RingHom.id_apply]
240	  exact congrArg f hsr
241	
242	/-- **Automorphism rigidity (ring form, `lm:aut`).**  A global function `u` on `C × T` whose
243	restriction along the section `σ` is `1` (`s u = 1`) is itself `1`, provided the comparison map
244	`f = π.appTop` is bijective and `s = σ.appTop` retracts it.  Downstream: a unit on `C × T`
245	rigidified to `1` along `σ` equals `1`. -/
246	theorem eq_one_of_isRetraction_of_restrict_eq_one {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
247	    (f : R →+* S) (s : S →+* R) (hf : Function.Bijective f)
248	    (hsf : s.comp f = RingHom.id R) (u : S) (hu : s u = 1) : u = 1 := by
249	  have h := eq_apply_of_isRetraction f s hf hsf u
250	  rw [hu, map_one] at h
251	  exact h.symm
252	
253	/-- A section `σ` of `π = pullback.snd C.hom πT` induces a retraction of the structure-sheaf
254	comparison map on global sections: `σ.appTop ∘ π.appTop = id`. -/
255	theorem retraction_appTop_of_section (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
256	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
257	    (σ : T ⟶ pullback C.hom πT) (hσ : σ ≫ pullback.snd C.hom πT = 𝟙 T) :
258	    (σ.appTop).hom.comp ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom = RingHom.id _ := by
259	  rw [← CommRingCat.hom_comp, ← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hσ]; simp
260	
261	/-- **Global functions on `C × T` are pulled back from `T`, uniquely (scheme form).**  Given the
262	field-of-constants comparison bijectivity `hbij` (P1 for `T = Spec A`, P2 for general `T`) and a
263	section `σ` of `π = pullback.snd C.hom πT`, every global function `u` on `C × T` equals the
264	pullback along `π` of its restriction `σ.appTop u` along the section. -/
265	theorem appTop_restrict_eq_of_section (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
266	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
267	    (hbij : Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom)
268	    (σ : T ⟶ pullback C.hom πT) (hσ : σ ≫ pullback.snd C.hom πT = 𝟙 T)
269	    (u : ↥Γ(pullback C.hom πT, ⊤)) :
270	    ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom ((σ.appTop).hom u) = u :=
271	  eq_apply_of_isRetraction _ _ hbij (retraction_appTop_of_section C πT σ hσ) u
272	
273	/-- **Automorphism rigidity for `C × T` (`lm:aut`, scheme form).**  Given the field-of-constants
274	comparison bijectivity `hbij` and a section `σ` of `π`, any global function `u` on `C × T` whose
275	restriction along `σ` is `1` equals `1` (Kleiman §2 rigidification of `Pic^♯`: a unit rigidified
276	to `1` along the identity section is trivial). -/
277	theorem eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
278	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
279	    (hbij : Function.Bijective ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop).hom)
280	    (σ : T ⟶ pullback C.hom πT) (hσ : σ ≫ pullback.snd C.hom πT = 𝟙 T)
281	    (u : ↥Γ(pullback C.hom πT, ⊤)) (hu : (σ.appTop).hom u = 1) : u = 1 :=
282	  eq_one_of_isRetraction_of_restrict_eq_one _ _ hbij
283	    (retraction_appTop_of_section C πT σ hσ) u hu
284	
285	/-- **Automorphism rigidity, gated form (`lm:aut`).**  For any base `T` supplying the P2 gate
286	`HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso`, a global function on `C × T` rigidified to `1` along a section
287	`σ` is `1`.  Unconditional for affine `T` (the gate instance is P1).  This is the reusable shape
288	Kleiman §2 uses to rigidify `Pic^♯`: a line-bundle automorphism restricting to the identity along
289	the identity section is the identity. -/
290	theorem eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one_of_gate (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
291	    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
292	    [HasStructureSheafPushforwardIso C πT]
293	    (σ : T ⟶ pullback C.hom πT) (hσ : σ ≫ pullback.snd C.hom πT = 𝟙 T)
294	    (u : ↥Γ(pullback C.hom πT, ⊤)) (hu : (σ.appTop).hom u = 1) : u = 1 :=
295	  eq_one_of_section_of_restrict_eq_one C πT
296	    (bijective_appTop_of_hasStructureSheafPushforwardIso C πT) σ hσ u hu

/-- Transport `IsIso (·.appTop)` across an isomorphism of arrows: given scheme morphisms
`a : W ⟶ X`, `b : Y ⟶ Z` and isomorphisms `l : W ≅ Y`, `r : X ≅ Z` forming a commuting square
`a ≫ r.hom = l.hom ≫ b`, if `b.appTop` is an isomorphism then so is `a.appTop`.  (The two ends of
the square being isomorphisms makes the induced global-section maps differ by isomorphisms.) -/
private lemma isIso_appTop_of_isoSq {W X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {a : W ⟶ X} {b : Y ⟶ Z}
    (l : W ≅ Y) (r : X ≅ Z) (comm : a ≫ r.hom = l.hom ≫ b) [IsIso (b.appTop)] :
    IsIso (a.appTop) := by
  have key := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop comm
  rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at key
  haveI : IsIso (r.hom.appTop) := isIso_appTop_of_isIso r.hom
  haveI : IsIso (l.hom.appTop) := isIso_appTop_of_isIso l.hom
  have ha : a.appTop = inv (r.hom.appTop) ≫ b.appTop ≫ l.hom.appTop := by
    rw [← key, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  rw [ha]; infer_instance

integral curve `C/k`, an arbitrary base `T` with structure map `πT : T ⟶ Spec k`, and any affine
open `V ⊆ T`, the structure-sheaf comparison `Γ(T, V) → Γ(C ×_k T, π⁻¹ V)`
(`π = pullback.snd C.hom πT`) is an isomorphism.  This is P1 at the affine base `V.toScheme`
(`bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine` with structure map `V.ι ≫ πT`) transported across the
identification `π ⁻¹ᵁ V ≅ C ×_k V` supplied by pullback pasting (`pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso`) and
the restriction-pullback isomorphism (`pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict`). -/
theorem isIso_snd_app_of_isAffineOpen (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    {V : T.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).app V) := by
  haveI : IsAffine V.toScheme := hV
  set π := pullback.snd C.hom πT with hπ
  -- P1 at the affine base `V.toScheme`, structure map `V.ι ≫ πT`.
  haveI hbase : IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom (V.ι ≫ πT)).appTop) :=
    (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr (bijective_snd_appTop_of_isAffine C (V.ι ≫ πT))
  -- Transport 1: the pasting iso `pullback π V.ι ≅ pullback C.hom (V.ι ≫ πT)`.
  haveI h1 : IsIso ((pullback.snd π V.ι).appTop) :=
    isIso_appTop_of_isoSq (b := pullback.snd C.hom (V.ι ≫ πT))
      (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso C.hom πT V.ι) (Iso.refl _) (by simp [hπ])
  -- Transport 2: the restriction-pullback iso `(π ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme ≅ pullback π V.ι`.
  haveI h2 : IsIso ((π ∣_ V).appTop) :=
    isIso_appTop_of_isoSq (b := pullback.snd π V.ι)

  -- Convert `(π ∣_ V).appTop` to `π.app V` via `morphismRestrict_appTop`.

theorem isIso_snd_appTop (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (πT : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :
    IsIso ((pullback.snd C.hom πT).appTop) := by
  set π := pullback.snd C.hom πT with hπ
  -- Package the presheaf-level comparison `π.c` as a morphism of sheaves of rings on `T`.
  let G := (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat π.base).obj (pullback C.hom πT).sheaf
  let α : T.sheaf ⟶ G := ⟨π.c⟩
  -- On every affine open the component is `π.app U`, an isomorphism by Step A.
  have hbasis : ∀ U ∈ T.affineOpens, IsIso (α.1.app (op U)) := fun U hU =>
    isIso_snd_app_of_isAffineOpen C πT hU
  have hinj : ∀ U ∈ T.affineOpens, Function.Injective (α.1.app (op U)) := fun U hU =>
    ((ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mp (hbasis U hU)).1
  -- Every stalk map of `α` is bijective, hence an isomorphism.
  haveI hstalk : ∀ x : ↑T,

    intro x
    rw [ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective]
    refine ⟨TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor_map_injective_of_isBasis
      T.isBasis_affineOpens hinj x, ?_⟩
